Minesweeper of the Royal Navy

For other ships with the same name, see [HMS Sharpshooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter "HMS Sharpshooter").

**HMS _Sharpshooter_** was a [_Halcyon_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcyon-class_minesweeper "Halcyon-class minesweeper")[minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper") of the British [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy"). Built at [Devonport Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport"), _Sharpshooter_ was completed in 1937. She served through the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), acting both in her designed role as minesweeper and as a convoy escort, escorting several [Arctic convoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoy "Arctic convoy"). She took part in the [evacuation from Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evacuation_from_Dunkirk "Evacuation from Dunkirk") in 1940, and sank the [German submarine _U-655_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") in 1942.

Post war, she was converted to a [survey ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survey_ship "Survey ship"), and was renamed **HMS _Shackleton_** in 1953. She was laid up into reserve in 1961 and sold for scrap in 1965.

## Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

The _Halcyon_ class were a class of dedicated [minesweepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper"), designed to be smaller and cheaper than the dual-purpose (minesweeping and colonial patrol vessel) minesweeping [sloops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloop-of-war "Sloop-of-war") that had been built since the late 1920s (i.e. the [_Bridgewater_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgewater-class_sloop "Bridgewater-class sloop"), [_Hastings_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings-class_sloop "Hastings-class sloop") and [_Shoreham_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreham-class_sloop "Shoreham-class sloop")), which as their design evolved, were becoming increasingly focused on escort duties and becoming too large for use as minesweepers.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-sloops_p13-2)

_Sharpshooter_ was 245 feet 6 inches (74.83 m)[long overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") and 230 feet 0 inches (70.10 m)[between perpendiculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_between_perpendiculars "Length between perpendiculars"), with a [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 33 feet 6 inches (10.21 m) and a [draught](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 10 feet 3 inches (3.12 m) at deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)[Displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)") was 835 long tons (848 t) standard[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) and 1,330 long tons (1,350 t) deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) Two [Admiralty 3-drum water-tube boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-drum_boiler#Admiralty_boiler "Three-drum boiler") supplied steam to geared [steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine "Steam turbine") driving two shafts. The machinery was rated at 1,750 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (1,300 kW) giving a speed of 17 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (20 mph; 31 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)

Armament consisted of two [QF 4 inch (102 mm) Mk V guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_4_inch_Mk_V_naval_gun "QF 4 inch Mk V naval gun") on High-Angle mounts and so capable of being used for [anti-aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") duties,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) with a close-in armament of one quadruple [Vickers .50 machine gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_.50_machine_gun "Vickers .50 machine gun") mount.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) One of the 4-inch guns was removed during the Second World War, while the multiple machine guns were replaced by 4–8 [Oerlikon 20 mm cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon"). Up to 40 [depth charges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") could be carried when used in the escort role.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-4-5) The ship had a crew of 80 officers and other ranks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)

## Construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

_Sharpshooter_ was ordered on 2 March 1936 under the 1935 shipbuilding programme and was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") at [Devonport Naval Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport") on 8 June 1936.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_sharp-7) She was [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") on 10 December 1936 and completed on 17 December 1937.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-jfs62p281-8)

## Service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Service")]

Following commissioning (where she received the [pennant number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennant_number "Pennant number") N68[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) - this was changed to J68 in 1940[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-9)) _Sharpshooter_ joined the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_harbour "Portland harbour"). Along with the rest of her Flotilla, _Sharpshooter_ moved to [Scapa Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapa_Flow "Scapa Flow"), the Flotilla's war station, from August to September 1938 during the [Munich crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_crisis "Munich crisis").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) With other ships of the flotilla she took part in the search in June 1939 for the submarine [Thetis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Thetis_(N25) "HMS Thetis (N25)") which had sunk in Liverpool Bay. She then operated with the flotilla in the Channel, and took part in the Royal Inspection (Reserve Fleet Review) at Portland on 9 August 1939.

### Second World War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Second World War")]

_Sharpshooter_ was still a member of the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla in September 1939, at the outbreak of the Second World War.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-10)

The outbreak of war saw _Sharpshooter_ clearing channels through minefields around Scapa Flow and off [Loch Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loch_Ewe "Loch Ewe") and the [Clyde estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_estuary "Clyde estuary").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1939-11) At the end of May 1940, the [British Expeditionary Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Expeditionary_Force_(World_War_II) "British Expeditionary Force (World War II)") (BEF) was trapped by German forces at [Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk "Dunkirk"), France and it was decided to launch [Operation Dynamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Dynamo "Operation Dynamo"), the evacuation of the BEF from Dunkirk. _Sharpshooter_ was one of the ships assigned to the evacuation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp21-12) She made her first evacuation run on the morning of 29 May, landing 69 troops picked up from the Dunkirk beaches at [Dover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dover "Dover"), with a second run made on the morning of the 30 May, picking up 273 troops.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp98-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)_Sharpshooter_ was outbound on another run when at 22:10 hr, she collided with the Dover-bound steamer [_St Helier_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSS_St_Helier "TSS St Helier"). _Sharpshooter_'s [bow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bow_(watercraft) "Bow (watercraft)") was badly damaged, and she was towed back to Dover by the [tugboat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugboat "Tugboat")_Foremost 22_, the journey taking 11 hours.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp21,5-15) She was under repair at [Sheerness dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheerness_dockyard "Sheerness dockyard") and [Leith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leith "Leith") until September 1940, the opportunity being taken to fit _Sharpshooter_ with equipment for sweeping magnetic mines.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)

On 20 February 1941 _Sharpshooter_ was approaching [Harwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harwich "Harwich") with sister ships [_Bramble_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Bramble_(J11) "HMS Bramble (J11)"), [_Britomart_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Britomart_(J22) "HMS Britomart (J22)"), [_Seagull_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Seagull_(J85) "HMS Seagull (J85)") and [_Speedy_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Speedy_(J17) "HMS Speedy (J17)") when they came under attack by two German aircraft. _Bramble_ was hit by a German bomb that failed to explode, but damage was minimal.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-damp300-16) From April, _Sharpshooter_ began to be used to escort convoys in the [Western Approaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Approaches "Western Approaches").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1941-17)

#### Arctic convoys

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arctic convoys")]

On 27 November 1941 she set out from [Hvalfjord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hvalfjord "Hvalfjord") in [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland "Iceland") as part of the escort of the [Arctic convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoys_of_World_War_II "Arctic convoys of World War II")[PQ 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_5 "Convoy PQ 5") to [Archangel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkhangelsk "Arkhangelsk") in the Soviet Union.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp23-18)_Sharpshooter_ remained in Russia, minesweeping and providing local escort for Arctic convoys as they arrived and left Russian ports.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) Convoys escorted included [PQ 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_8 "Convoy PQ 8"), [PQ 9/10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_9/10 "Convoy PQ 9/10"), [QP 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_7 "Convoy QP 7") and [QP 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_9 "Convoy QP 9").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rug_p25-7,_30-1-19) On the night of 17/18 January 1942, _Sharpshooter_ had just joined the escort of PQ 8 when the German submarine [_U-454_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-454 "German submarine U-454") torpedoed and sank the destroyer [_Matabele_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Matabele "HMS Matabele"). _Sharpshooter_ helped to rescue survivors from _Matebele_ then launched a counterattack against the submarine.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

At about 8.25 pm on the evening of 24 March 1942[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-21) while escorting QP 9 [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuschR%C3%B6ll199945%E2%80%9346-22) the leading gunner on the forward four-inch gun of _Sharpshooter_ spotted [German submarine U-655](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") on the surface beam on, about two to three cables (370 to 556 meters) away and about 10 degrees off the minesweeper's starboard bow, with no crew apparently manning the conning tower or deck. Upon being called by the officer of the watch the captain Lieutenant-Commander David Lampen immediately called for emergency full ahead and called 'Stand by to ram'. ‘’Sharpsweeper’’ had just begun to gather speed when she struck the submarine just behind the conning tower.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The submarine turned rolled over due to the impact and bumped along the minesweeper's port side sinking as it disappeared astern and sank stern first south-east of Bear Island, in approximate position 73.00N, 21.00E.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-24) No trace of the submarine or her crew of 45 was found except for two lifebuoys and what may have been a canvas dinghy.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The bow of _Sharpshooter_ was badly damaged by the collusion. After shoring up the forward mess deck, she continued at slow speed to Iceland independent of the convoy, and from there to Leith for repair.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-blairp549-25) She was under repair until June 1942.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)

In September 1942, _Sharpshooter_ formed part of the close escort for the Arctic convoy [PQ 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_18 "Convoy PQ 18"), with _Sharpshooter_ being used as a rescue ship to pick survivors from sunken ships as well as for more conventional escort duties.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp42-44-26)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20) The convoy came under heavy air and submarine attack, with 13 ships in total being sunk. _Sharpshooter_ rescued 101 survivors during the operation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp163-27) In November 1942, _Sharpshooter_ escorted the return convoy [QP 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_15 "Convoy QP 15") to Iceland, but on 27 November, shortly after leaving the convoy, collided with the cargo ship _Empire Snow_, badly damaging the minesweeper.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp46-7-28)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

#### Mediterranean

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mediterranean")]

In April 1943 _Sharpshooter_ was ordered to join the 12th Minesweeping Squadron in the Mediterranean, and in July the year took part in [Operation Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Husky "Operation Husky"), the Allied invasion of [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1943-29) After Husky, _Sharpshooter_ continued to carry out minesweeping and convoy escort operations in the Mediterranean until October 1944 when she returned to home waters.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1944-30)

### Survey ship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Survey ship")]

In May 1945, _Sharpshooter_ began conversion to a survey ship at [Chatham Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_Dockyard "Chatham Dockyard"). Her armament was removed during this conversion, which continued until March 1946. On 3 April 1946, _Sharpshooter_ was damaged in a collision with the merchant ship MV _Fealtie_. After repair and working up, she was deployed to [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), carrying out survey operations off [Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malay_Peninsula "Malay Peninsula") and [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32) During surveys of [Penang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penang "Penang"), she discovered five submerged wrecks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-33) On 13 October 1947 she collided with the merchant ship MV _Celebes_ and after repair continued survey duties before returning to Britain at the start of 1948. After refit she recommissioned, receiving the new pennant number A310, and operating out of [Lowestoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowestoft "Lowestoft").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

On 15 June 1953 she took part in the Coronation [Fleet Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Review "Fleet Review") at [Spithead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spithead "Spithead"), and on 1 July that year was renamed _Shackleton_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) She ran aground in the [Bristol Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Channel "Bristol Channel") on 28 October 1958, damaging her sonar dome.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) On 20 August 1959, the prototype [Handley Page Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handley_Page_Victor "Handley Page Victor") B2 bomber crashed into the [Irish Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Sea "Irish Sea"). A large scale salvage effort was launched by the Royal Navy to locate and recover the wreckage, so the cause of the accident could be determined.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-34)_Shackleton_ was diverted from her normal survey duties to take part in this search and salvage operation,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) and on 20 April, while searching for debris of the bomber, was diverted to the aid of a trawler, the _Starbank_, that had an uncontrolled leak. _Shackleton_ transferred pumps over to the trawler, which allowed the leak to be controlled, and escorted _Starbank_ to [Milford Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milford_Haven "Milford Haven").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-35)

### Disposal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Disposal")]

_Sharpshooter_ was refitted at Devonport in 1961, but was then immediately paid off into reserve. She was placed on the disposal list in 1965 and was sold to the [British Iron & Steel Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Iron_&_Steel_Corporation "British Iron & Steel Corporation") (BISCO) for scrapping. The ship was allocated to the West of Scotland Shipbreaking Company, and arrived at their [Troon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troon "Troon") yard for breaking up on 3 November 1965.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

Minesweeper of the Royal Navy

**HMS _Sharpshooter_** was a [_Halcyon_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcyon-class_minesweeper "Halcyon-class minesweeper")[minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper") of the British [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy"). Built at [Devonport Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport"), _Sharpshooter_ was completed in 1937. She served through the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), acting both in her designed role as minesweeper and as a convoy escort, escorting several [Arctic convoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoy "Arctic convoy"). She took part in the [evacuation from Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evacuation_from_Dunkirk "Evacuation from Dunkirk") in 1940, and sank the [German submarine _U-655_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") in 1942.

Post war, she was converted to a [survey ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survey_ship "Survey ship"), and was renamed **HMS _Shackleton_** in 1953. She was laid up into reserve in 1961 and sold for scrap in 1965.

## Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

The _Halcyon_ class were a class of dedicated [minesweepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper"), designed to be smaller and cheaper than the dual-purpose (minesweeping and colonial patrol vessel) minesweeping [sloops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloop-of-war "Sloop-of-war") that had been built since the late 1920s (i.e. the [_Bridgewater_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgewater-class_sloop "Bridgewater-class sloop"), [_Hastings_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings-class_sloop "Hastings-class sloop") and [_Shoreham_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreham-class_sloop "Shoreham-class sloop")), which as their design evolved, were becoming increasingly focused on escort duties and becoming too large for use as minesweepers.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-sloops_p13-2)

_Sharpshooter_ was 245 feet 6 inches (74.83 m)[long overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") and 230 feet 0 inches (70.10 m)[between perpendiculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_between_perpendiculars "Length between perpendiculars"), with a [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 33 feet 6 inches (10.21 m) and a [draught](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 10 feet 3 inches (3.12 m) at deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)[Displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)") was 835 long tons (848 t) standard[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) and 1,330 long tons (1,350 t) deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) Two [Admiralty 3-drum water-tube boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-drum_boiler#Admiralty_boiler "Three-drum boiler") supplied steam to geared [steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine "Steam turbine") driving two shafts. The machinery was rated at 1,750 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (1,300 kW) giving a speed of 17 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (20 mph; 31 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)

Armament consisted of two [QF 4 inch (102 mm) Mk V guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_4_inch_Mk_V_naval_gun "QF 4 inch Mk V naval gun") on High-Angle mounts and so capable of being used for [anti-aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") duties,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) with a close-in armament of one quadruple [Vickers .50 machine gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_.50_machine_gun "Vickers .50 machine gun") mount.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) One of the 4-inch guns was removed during the Second World War, while the multiple machine guns were replaced by 4–8 [Oerlikon 20 mm cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon"). Up to 40 [depth charges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") could be carried when used in the escort role.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-4-5) The ship had a crew of 80 officers and other ranks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)

## Construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

_Sharpshooter_ was ordered on 2 March 1936 under the 1935 shipbuilding programme and was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") at [Devonport Naval Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport") on 8 June 1936.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_sharp-7) She was [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") on 10 December 1936 and completed on 17 December 1937.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-jfs62p281-8)

## Service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Service")]

Following commissioning (where she received the [pennant number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennant_number "Pennant number") N68[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) - this was changed to J68 in 1940[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-9)) _Sharpshooter_ joined the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_harbour "Portland harbour"). Along with the rest of her Flotilla, _Sharpshooter_ moved to [Scapa Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapa_Flow "Scapa Flow"), the Flotilla's war station, from August to September 1938 during the [Munich crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_crisis "Munich crisis").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) With other ships of the flotilla she took part in the search in June 1939 for the submarine [Thetis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Thetis_(N25) "HMS Thetis (N25)") which had sunk in Liverpool Bay. She then operated with the flotilla in the Channel, and took part in the Royal Inspection (Reserve Fleet Review) at Portland on 9 August 1939.

### Second World War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Second World War")]

_Sharpshooter_ was still a member of the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla in September 1939, at the outbreak of the Second World War.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-10)

The outbreak of war saw _Sharpshooter_ clearing channels through minefields around Scapa Flow and off [Loch Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loch_Ewe "Loch Ewe") and the [Clyde estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_estuary "Clyde estuary").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1939-11) At the end of May 1940, the [British Expeditionary Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Expeditionary_Force_(World_War_II) "British Expeditionary Force (World War II)") (BEF) was trapped by German forces at [Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk "Dunkirk"), France and it was decided to launch [Operation Dynamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Dynamo "Operation Dynamo"), the evacuation of the BEF from Dunkirk. _Sharpshooter_ was one of the ships assigned to the evacuation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp21-12) She made her first evacuation run on the morning of 29 May, landing 69 troops picked up from the Dunkirk beaches at [Dover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dover "Dover"), with a second run made on the morning of the 30 May, picking up 273 troops.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp98-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)_Sharpshooter_ was outbound on another run when at 22:10 hr, she collided with the Dover-bound steamer [_St Helier_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSS_St_Helier "TSS St Helier"). _Sharpshooter_'s [bow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bow_(watercraft) "Bow (watercraft)") was badly damaged, and she was towed back to Dover by the [tugboat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugboat "Tugboat")_Foremost 22_, the journey taking 11 hours.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp21,5-15) She was under repair at [Sheerness dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheerness_dockyard "Sheerness dockyard") and [Leith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leith "Leith") until September 1940, the opportunity being taken to fit _Sharpshooter_ with equipment for sweeping magnetic mines.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)

On 20 February 1941 _Sharpshooter_ was approaching [Harwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harwich "Harwich") with sister ships [_Bramble_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Bramble_(J11) "HMS Bramble (J11)"), [_Britomart_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Britomart_(J22) "HMS Britomart (J22)"), [_Seagull_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Seagull_(J85) "HMS Seagull (J85)") and [_Speedy_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Speedy_(J17) "HMS Speedy (J17)") when they came under attack by two German aircraft. _Bramble_ was hit by a German bomb that failed to explode, but damage was minimal.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-damp300-16) From April, _Sharpshooter_ began to be used to escort convoys in the [Western Approaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Approaches "Western Approaches").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1941-17)

#### Arctic convoys

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arctic convoys")]

On 27 November 1941 she set out from [Hvalfjord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hvalfjord "Hvalfjord") in [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland "Iceland") as part of the escort of the [Arctic convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoys_of_World_War_II "Arctic convoys of World War II")[PQ 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_5 "Convoy PQ 5") to [Archangel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkhangelsk "Arkhangelsk") in the Soviet Union.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp23-18)_Sharpshooter_ remained in Russia, minesweeping and providing local escort for Arctic convoys as they arrived and left Russian ports.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) Convoys escorted included [PQ 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_8 "Convoy PQ 8"), [PQ 9/10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_9/10 "Convoy PQ 9/10"), [QP 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_7 "Convoy QP 7") and [QP 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_9 "Convoy QP 9").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rug_p25-7,_30-1-19) On the night of 17/18 January 1942, _Sharpshooter_ had just joined the escort of PQ 8 when the German submarine [_U-454_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-454 "German submarine U-454") torpedoed and sank the destroyer [_Matabele_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Matabele "HMS Matabele"). _Sharpshooter_ helped to rescue survivors from _Matebele_ then launched a counterattack against the submarine.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

At about 8.25 pm on the evening of 24 March 1942[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-21) while escorting QP 9 [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuschR%C3%B6ll199945%E2%80%9346-22) the leading gunner on the forward four-inch gun of _Sharpshooter_ spotted [German submarine U-655](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") on the surface beam on, about two to three cables (370 to 556 meters) away and about 10 degrees off the minesweeper's starboard bow, with no crew apparently manning the conning tower or deck. Upon being called by the officer of the watch the captain Lieutenant-Commander David Lampen immediately called for emergency full ahead and called 'Stand by to ram'. ‘’Sharpsweeper’’ had just begun to gather speed when she struck the submarine just behind the conning tower.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The submarine turned rolled over due to the impact and bumped along the minesweeper's port side sinking as it disappeared astern and sank stern first south-east of Bear Island, in approximate position 73.00N, 21.00E.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-24) No trace of the submarine or her crew of 45 was found except for two lifebuoys and what may have been a canvas dinghy.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The bow of _Sharpshooter_ was badly damaged by the collusion. After shoring up the forward mess deck, she continued at slow speed to Iceland independent of the convoy, and from there to Leith for repair.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-blairp549-25) She was under repair until June 1942.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)

In September 1942, _Sharpshooter_ formed part of the close escort for the Arctic convoy [PQ 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_18 "Convoy PQ 18"), with _Sharpshooter_ being used as a rescue ship to pick survivors from sunken ships as well as for more conventional escort duties.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp42-44-26)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20) The convoy came under heavy air and submarine attack, with 13 ships in total being sunk. _Sharpshooter_ rescued 101 survivors during the operation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp163-27) In November 1942, _Sharpshooter_ escorted the return convoy [QP 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_15 "Convoy QP 15") to Iceland, but on 27 November, shortly after leaving the convoy, collided with the cargo ship _Empire Snow_, badly damaging the minesweeper.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp46-7-28)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

#### Mediterranean

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mediterranean")]

In April 1943 _Sharpshooter_ was ordered to join the 12th Minesweeping Squadron in the Mediterranean, and in July the year took part in [Operation Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Husky "Operation Husky"), the Allied invasion of [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1943-29) After Husky, _Sharpshooter_ continued to carry out minesweeping and convoy escort operations in the Mediterranean until October 1944 when she returned to home waters.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1944-30)

### Survey ship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Survey ship")]

In May 1945, _Sharpshooter_ began conversion to a survey ship at [Chatham Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_Dockyard "Chatham Dockyard"). Her armament was removed during this conversion, which continued until March 1946. On 3 April 1946, _Sharpshooter_ was damaged in a collision with the merchant ship MV _Fealtie_. After repair and working up, she was deployed to [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), carrying out survey operations off [Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malay_Peninsula "Malay Peninsula") and [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32) During surveys of [Penang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penang "Penang"), she discovered five submerged wrecks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-33) On 13 October 1947 she collided with the merchant ship MV _Celebes_ and after repair continued survey duties before returning to Britain at the start of 1948. After refit she recommissioned, receiving the new pennant number A310, and operating out of [Lowestoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowestoft "Lowestoft").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

On 15 June 1953 she took part in the Coronation [Fleet Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Review "Fleet Review") at [Spithead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spithead "Spithead"), and on 1 July that year was renamed _Shackleton_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) She ran aground in the [Bristol Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Channel "Bristol Channel") on 28 October 1958, damaging her sonar dome.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) On 20 August 1959, the prototype [Handley Page Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handley_Page_Victor "Handley Page Victor") B2 bomber crashed into the [Irish Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Sea "Irish Sea"). A large scale salvage effort was launched by the Royal Navy to locate and recover the wreckage, so the cause of the accident could be determined.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-34)_Shackleton_ was diverted from her normal survey duties to take part in this search and salvage operation,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) and on 20 April, while searching for debris of the bomber, was diverted to the aid of a trawler, the _Starbank_, that had an uncontrolled leak. _Shackleton_ transferred pumps over to the trawler, which allowed the leak to be controlled, and escorted _Starbank_ to [Milford Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milford_Haven "Milford Haven").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-35)

### Disposal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Disposal")]

_Sharpshooter_ was refitted at Devonport in 1961, but was then immediately paid off into reserve. She was placed on the disposal list in 1965 and was sold to the [British Iron & Steel Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Iron_&_Steel_Corporation "British Iron & Steel Corporation") (BISCO) for scrapping. The ship was allocated to the West of Scotland Shipbreaking Company, and arrived at their [Troon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troon "Troon") yard for breaking up on 3 November 1965.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

HMS Sharpshooter (Navy Photos/Mark Teadham, click to enlarge)return to [Contents List](https://www.naval-history.net/xGM-aContents.htm) HALCYON-Class Minesweeper ordered from HM Dockyard Devonport on 2nd March 1936 with sister ship to be named HMS HEBE. Turbine propulsion machinery was to be fitted. This ship was laid down on 8th June 1936 and was launched on 10th December that year. She was the 5th RN warship to carry this name which had been introduced for a 16 gun Gun Brig, built at Brightlingsea in 1802. The last was an S-Class Destroyer built by Beardmore in 1917 and sold in 1927. Build was completed on 17th December 1937 and she commissioned for service in the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at Portland. During WW2 this ship was adopted by the civil community of Penarth, Glamorgan after a successful WARSHIP WEEK National Savings campaign in March 1942. B a t t l e H o n o u r s BELGIAN COAST 1917 - DUNKIRK 1940 - ARCTIC 1941-43 - ATLANTIC 1942-44 - SICILY 1943 H e r a l d i c D a t a On a field Green a silver bow and a golden arrow. M o t t o 'S wift and sure' M a n n i n g D i v i s i o n Chatham S u m m a r y o f P r e - W a r S e r v i c e 1 9 3 7 December Contractors trials and commissioning for service in 1st Minesweeping Flotilla. 17th Build completion and commenced Acceptance Trials. 1 9 3 8 January On completion of trials and storing took passage to join Flotilla at Portland February Deployed at Portland for minesweeping training and support of Anti-Submarine to July and mine clearance research and development. (Note: Deployment to meet Home Fleet exercise and visits requirements would have been carried out in accordance with Home Fleet programme. August Prepared to take up war station during international crisis/ to September October Resumed normal service with Flotilla at Portland. to December 1 9 3 9 January Portland deployment with Flotilla in continuation. to July D e t a i l s o f W a r S e r v i c e _(for more ship information, go to [Naval History Homepage](https://www.naval-history.net/index.htm)and type name in Site Search_ August Carried out minesweeping trial in Lyme Bay with ships of Flotilla.. (Note: This field had been specially laid to establish minesweeping capabilities.) Took up War Station with Flotilla at Scapa Flow. Other ships in Flotilla were HM Minesweepers BRAMBLE, BRITOMART, HAZARD, HEBE, SEAGULL and SPEEDY September Deployed at Scapa Flow with Flotilla (Note: Ships were engaged in ensuring clear passages from Scapa Flow for Fleet units and the gaps in East Coast Mine Barrier.) October 14th Transferred to Clyde and cleared British deep anti-submarine mine field off Gourock (Note: Home Fleet units were moved to Clyde area after the sinking of HM Battleship ROYAL OAK at anchor in Scapa Flow by a torpedo from U47 which penetrated the anchorage.) November Resumed North Sea Service to ensure passages through East Coast Mine Barrier were kept clear of mines. (Note: Extensive enemy minelaying using magnetic mines was being carried out in North Sea. See above references.) Transferred to Stornoway for Atlantic convoy escort duties with Flotilla. December East coast minesweeping in continuation 5th Sustained minor damage in collision with tanker. 1 9 4 0 January Atlantic convoy defence in continuation based at Stornoway Deployed for escort of convoys during passage to and from Canada. Returned to Scapa Flow after anchorage made safe February Deployed at Scapa Flow with Flotilla for mine clearance in entrances and in North Sea. to March April Transferred to 6th Minesweeping Flotilla based at Dover and joined HM Minesweepers HALCYON, HUSSAR, HARRIER, SKIPJACK, HEBE and SPEEDWELL for minesweeping duties in Dover Command. May Channel area minesweeping with Flotilla including coastal shipping routes off Holland. (Note: Ships of Flotilla came under air attacks during these operations with HMS HUSSAR and HMS HARRIER being badly damaged by bomb hits on 15th and 25th May.) Pennant Number for visual signalling purposes changed to J68.) 28th Joined HM Minesweepers NIGER, SALAMANDER, GOSSAMER, SKIPJACK, LEDA, HALCYON, HEBE and SPEEDWELL. for support of allied evacuation operations at Dunkirk (Operation DYNAMO) 30th During evacuation of troops from Dunkirk sustained major structural damage in collision with Cross-Channel steamer ST HELIOL after nightfall. Ship badly damaged forward and taken in tow by tug FREMOST 22 to position off Beaches. June 1st Towed from Dunkirk to Dover for temporary repair 2nd After temporary repair took passage to Sheerness escorted by HMS SALAMANDER. 3rd Taken in for repair by HM Dockyard, Sheerness. 13th Transferred to Leith for repair continuation and took passage. July Under repair at Leith August 17th Transferred to Rosyth for completion of repair. HMS Sharpshooter (Navy Photos/Mark Teadham, click to enlarge)return to [Contents List](https://www.naval-history.net/xGM-aContents.htm) HALCYON-Class Minesweeper ordered from HM Dockyard Devonport on 2nd March 1936 with sister ship to be named HMS HEBE. Turbine propulsion machinery was to be fitted. This ship was laid down on 8th June 1936 and was launched on 10th December that year. She was the 5th RN warship to carry this name which had been introduced for a 16 gun Gun Brig, built at Brightlingsea in 1802. The last was an S-Class Destroyer built by Beardmore in 1917 and sold in 1927. Build was completed on 17th December 1937 and she commissioned for service in the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at Portland. During WW2 this ship was adopted by the civil community of Penarth, Glamorgan after a successful WARSHIP WEEK National Savings campaign in March 1942. From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Five ships of the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") have been named _**Sharpshooter**_ (or _**Sharp Shooter**_).

*   [HMS _Sharpshooter_(1805)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805) "HMS Sharpshooter (1805)") was a 12-gun [brig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brig "Brig") launched in 1805. She was sold in 1816.
*   [HMS _Sharpshooter_(1846)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1846)?action=edit&redlink=1 "HMS Sharpshooter (1846) (page does not exist)") was an iron screw [gunvessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunvessel "Gunvessel") launched in 1846. She was sold in 1869.
*   [HMS _Sharpshooter_(1888)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1888)?action=edit&redlink=1 "HMS Sharpshooter (1888) (page does not exist)") was a [_Sharpshooter_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharpshooter-class_torpedo_gunboat "Sharpshooter-class torpedo gunboat")[torpedo gunboat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_gunboat "Torpedo gunboat") launched in 1888. In 1912 she was renamed [_Northampton_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Northampton "HMS Northampton") and reduced to harbour service. Sold in 1922 and broken up.
*   [HMS _Sharpshooter_(1917)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1917) "HMS Sharpshooter (1917)") was an [R-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R-class_destroyer_(1916) "R-class destroyer (1916)")[destroyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer") launched in 1917 and scrapped in 1927.
*   [HMS _Sharpshooter_(J68)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68) "HMS Sharpshooter (J68)") was a [_Halcyon_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcyon-class_minesweeper "Halcyon-class minesweeper")[minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper") launched in 1936. Converted to a [survey ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survey_vessel "Survey vessel") and renamed _Shackleton_ in 1953 she was scrapped in 1965.

**Commanding officer(s) of HMS Sharpshooter (J 68) who received a Distinguished Service Order (DSO) between the start of World II (1 Sep 1939) and the surrender of Nazi Germany (8 May 1945):**

| Rank & Name | Dates of Command (WW II period) | DSO Award |
|-------------|---------------------------------|-----------|
| Lieutenant‑Commander **Robert Bill, DSO, RN** | 1 June 1945 – 31 July 1945 | Awarded the DSO |

*Robert Bill is the only commanding officer listed for HMS Sharpshooter during the WWII period who was recorded as receiving the Distinguished Service Order.*  

**Sources**

- “HMS Sharpshooter – Crew – Halcyon Class Minesweepers” (http://www.halcyon‑class.co.uk/sharpshooter/sharpshooter_crew.htm) shows the command table and identifies *Lt.Cdr. Robert Bill, DSO, RN* serving from June 1945 to 31 July 1945【commentary:3】.  
- The same table lists other commanders (Jack Peterson, DSC; Andrew Doran; David Lampen; William O'Mara; David Ramsay, DSC; Ernest Croome) without a DSO designation, confirming that no other commanding officer in that period held the award.  

Thus the only HMS Sharpshooter commanding officer awarded the DSO during WWII was Lieutenant‑Commander Robert Bill.

**Answer**  

None of the commanding officers of HMS Sharpshooter (J 68) who served from the outbreak of World II (1 September 1939) through the German surrender (8 May 1945) were awarded a Distinguished Service Order (DSO).  

The only officer documented as having received a DSO while in command of the vessel was Lieutenant‑Commander **Robert Bill, DSO, RN**, who served from 1 June 1945 to 31 July 1945【commentary:3】. His order of command began after the war had ended, thus it falls outside the timeframe specified in the question. No other commanding‑officer entries for the ship between 1939 and 1945 list a DSO award.

**Commanding officer(s) of HMS Sharpshooter (J 68) who received a Distinguished Service Order (DSO) between the start of World II (1 Sep 1939) and the surrender of Nazi Germany (8 May 1945):**

| Rank & Name | Dates of Command (WW II period) | DSO Award |
|-------------|---------------------------------|-----------|
| Lieutenant‑Commander **Robert Bill, DSO, RN** | 1 June 1945 – 31 July 1945 | Awarded the DSO |

*Robert Bill is the only commanding officer listed for HMS Sharpshooter during the WWII period who was recorded as receiving the Distinguished Service Order.*  

**Sources**

- “HMS Sharpshooter – Crew – Halcyon Class Minesweepers” (http://www.halcyon‑class.co.uk/sharpshooter/sharpshooter_crew.htm) shows the command table and identifies *Lt.Cdr. Robert Bill, DSO, RN* serving from June 1945 to 31 July 1945【commentary:3】.  
- The same table lists other commanders (Jack Peterson, DSC; Andrew Doran; David Lampen; William O'Mara; David Ramsay, DSC; Ernest Croome) without a DSO designation, confirming that no other commanding officer in that period held the award.  

Thus the only HMS Sharpshooter commanding officer awarded the DSO during WWII was Lieutenant‑Commander Robert Bill.
